Updated CCPA regulations on automated decisionmaking technology

The California Privacy Protection Agency Board adopted regulations that require businesses to assess the risks of processing personal information, to complete cybersecurity audits, and to give consumers notice and a way to opt out when automated decisionmaking technology is used for significant decisions.

The regulations take effect on January 1, 2026. Businesses have until later dates to complete the first risk assessments and cybersecurity audits.

Who must comply

The regulations apply to businesses that are subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act and meet the thresholds the Act sets.
